house_rules: Payloads below are transcribed from the public record and attributed per entry - this corpus never invents payloads.
alert(1) in a probe stands for the operator's canary marker (MYTHOS-CANARY-<uuid>) at execution time - never ship alert() theater (organ doctrine).
Context first: a payload is only valid for the sink context it was written for; classify the context (references/contexts.md) BEFORE choosing an entry.
failure_modes are mandatory reading BEFORE closing a hypothesis as negative: a payload that failed for a listed reason leaves the sink untested, not safe.

entries.technique: HTML body context - element with inline event handler
prerequisites: reflection/insertion into HTML body element position
entries.oracle: marker executes on load; body artifact shows the element surviving into the DOM
failure_modes: CSP script-src without 'unsafe-inline' (or with nonce/hash) blocks the inline handler - the injection succeeded, execution did not: record CSP as the limiting fact
input filtered for < or specific tags - switch context class, do not spray variants
sanitizer strips the element on output - re-test via mutation entries (XSS-007..010) before concluding safe

prerequisites: insertion inside a double-quoted attribute value
entries.oracle: quote closes the attribute, new element parses; marker executes on image error
failure_modes: output encoding escapes the quote (") - the context is closed properly; encode-then-store flows re-encode on render
unquoted/single-quoted attribute contexts need their own breakout - verify the actual quoting byte first

entries.technique: unquoted attribute context / attribute injection without breakout
prerequisites: insertion after an unquoted attribute value or into a tag's attribute area
entries.oracle: focus fires on load without any user interaction; no quote breakout needed
failure_modes: CSP blocks inline handlers (same as XSS-001)
the insertion point quotes or escapes the space between tokens - the second attribute never parses

prerequisites: insertion inside a JS string literal in a script block
entries.oracle: string concatenation splices the marker call between string literals; executes when the statement runs
failure_modes: output JSON-encodes into the string (quotes escaped) - the literal stays closed
the block never executes (dead code / conditional) - execution context must be verified, not assumed

source.title: PortSwigger XSS cheat sheet (JS context vectors)

prerequisites: insertion inside a <script> block (raw text element)
entries.oracle: the closing tag ends the raw-text context whatever the string state inside; following markup parses as HTML
failure_modes: encoder escapes < to < inside script text (correct behavior - raw text rules make this rare but stack-dependent)
JSON-P callbacks that re-wrap the value - the breakout lands inside a JS string in ANOTHER script block; re-classify context

prerequisites: insertion into href/src/action or a redirect target
entries.oracle: navigation executes script under the origin; the // comments out any trailing template text
failure_modes: CSP (e.g. script-src, or object-src/srcset rules) or a scheme allowlist on the sink
framework sanitizes URLs (Angular sanitizer, DOMPurify URI validation)
sink is never navigated by a user gesture - impact requires a trigger path; note it in the report instead of assuming

prerequisites: sanitized output assigned via innerHTML in a scripting-enabled browser
sanitizer parses the payload inside <noscript> as inert text
entries.oracle: on re-parse in the live document the noscript content model flips (scripting enabled = raw text), the title attribute's markup executes as real nodes: the img lands OUTSIDE noscript and fires
failure_modes: target is a no-script or server-side render path - the mutation never triggers
modern sanitizer double-parse (parse-after-serialize verification) catches the mutation - pin the sanitizer version as a ledgered fact before retrying variants
mutation is engine-specific - record which engine verified the mutation, do not generalize across browsers

entries.oracle: HTML-in-SVG parse mutates the tree on serialize/re-parse; the style raw-text content re-interprets, the img escapes and executes
failure_modes: DOMPurify patched (>2.0.0 chain of fixes) - version-pin the sink before claiming the class is closed
sink is not a serialize/re-parse pipeline (direct DOM fragment insertion) - mutation window absent

entries.technique: mXSS - MathML form-pointer namespace confusion (DOMPurify 2.0.17 bypass)
prerequisites: DOMPurify up to 2.0.17 with default config, innerHTML sink
entries.oracle: the mis-nested </form> resets the form element pointer so the second <form> parses INSIDE math/mtext; serialization re-orders namespaces and the style content re-parses as HTML - img executes
failure_modes: fixed in DOMPurify >2.0.17 - this exact payload is a version ORACLE: its failure dates the sink's sanitizer, which is itself a ledgered FACT
no form-pointer behavior in the live engine (spec-conformant parser required) - engine-specific

entries.technique: mXSS - MathML mtext/table/mglyph/style with comment nesting (DOMPurify 2.0.17 bypass)
prerequisites: DOMPurify up to 2.0.17, innerHTML sink, HTML comment handling in play
entries.oracle: mglyph puts the parser in a state where style content mutates through a comment re-serialization; the title attribute value re-parses as markup - the inner img fires
failure_modes: fixed in later DOMPurify - same version-oracle property as XSS-009
the HTML-entity encoded title only mutates in engines that decode entities during attribute re-parse - verify per engine

entries.oracle: the legacy engine treats backticks as attribute delimiters - the onerror attribute parses as separate from src
failure_modes: modern engines never treat backticks as quotes - class is dead except on legacy enterprise targets; record the engine version if it fires
